subject.title: Cron Jobs Calendar View for Control UI

question: Should OpenClaw accept a repaired 24-hour Cron Jobs timeline as the first product slice, or require a fuller daily/week calendar design before implementation continues?
rationale: The remaining work is a Control UI product-scope choice, not a broken existing contract, and the open PR covers only part of the requested calendar/timeline behavior while needing a rebase onto current UI architecture.

options.title: Repair Narrow Timeline First
options.body: Rebase or replace the linked PR on the current cron page, preserve existing contracts, and accept the 24-hour timeline as the first slice while tracking or rejecting broader calendar features separately.

options.title: Design Full Calendar Scope
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define the daily, weekly, stats, and drag-and-drop editing behavior as one cohesive product direction.

options.title: Decline Core Calendar View
options.body: Close this issue and the linked PR after deciding the current list/run-history UI is sufficient for core.

recommendation.title: Repair Narrow Timeline First
recommendation.body: Rebase or replace the linked PR on the current cron page, preserve existing contracts, and accept the 24-hour timeline as the first slice while tracking or rejecting broader calendar features separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Control UI cron history and broader UI/product-surface work make this the strongest routing signal for the product-scope decision.
